title: Risk breakdown by attribution status
one_line_definition: This table breaks down RAF risk scores, gap capture performance, and open coding opportunities by member churn status (e.g., retained, new, churned), comparing current-year values to the prior year.
result_meaning: Analysts use this table to identify which member churn segments are driving risk documentation gaps or recapture gains, enabling targeted outreach and coding improvement strategies.

Eligible population.definition: The count of members attributed to the plan within each churn status segment who are eligible for risk adjustment in the measurement period.
Eligible population.increasing: Rising membership in a segment expands the risk adjustment opportunity and may dilute or amplify aggregate RAF scores depending on the mix of new versus retained members.
Eligible population.decreasing: Falling membership signals member attrition or attribution loss in that churn segment, which may reduce total risk revenue and limit the pool available for gap closure.

Documented risk.definition: The aggregate RAF score derived from HCC conditions that have already been coded and submitted for members in each churn status segment.
Documented risk.increasing: Higher documented risk indicates more chronic conditions are being captured and coded, supporting accurate risk-based reimbursement for that segment.
Documented risk.decreasing: Lower documented risk suggests coding gaps, member health improvement, or loss of high-acuity members, potentially signaling under-documentation and revenue leakage.

Gap to potential risk.definition: The difference between the maximum potential RAF score (based on suspected or historical HCCs) and the currently documented RAF score, representing uncaptured risk opportunity for each churn segment.
Gap to potential risk.increasing: A growing gap signals that more conditions are going uncoded relative to clinical evidence, indicating worsening documentation performance or an influx of members with unaddressed chronic conditions.
Gap to potential risk.decreasing: A shrinking gap indicates successful closure of coding opportunities, meaning care teams are effectively recapturing suspected or lapsed HCCs for that segment.

RAF recapture rate.definition: The percentage of the prior-year RAF score that has been successfully re-documented in the current year for members in each churn status segment, measuring year-over-year HCC continuity.
RAF recapture rate.increasing: A higher recapture rate means a greater proportion of previously coded conditions are being re-documented, reducing RAF erosion and stabilizing risk-based revenue.
RAF recapture rate.decreasing: A lower recapture rate indicates that previously coded HCCs are not being re-confirmed, leading to RAF score decay and potential reimbursement shortfalls.

RAF recapture rate YoY.definition: The year-over-year percentage change in the RAF recapture rate for each churn status segment, showing whether HCC re-documentation performance is improving or deteriorating.
RAF recapture rate YoY.increasing: A positive YoY change signals that the plan is getting better at re-documenting prior-year conditions, reflecting improved coding workflows or provider engagement.
RAF recapture rate YoY.decreasing: A negative YoY change warns that recapture performance is declining compared to the prior year, requiring intervention to prevent compounding RAF score erosion.

Risk recapture rate.definition: The percentage of total identified risk gaps (suspected and dropped HCCs) that have been successfully closed through documented coding for members in each churn status segment.
Risk recapture rate.increasing: A higher rate reflects effective gap closure efforts, meaning care managers and coders are successfully converting suspected conditions into confirmed, submitted diagnoses.
Risk recapture rate.decreasing: A lower rate indicates that identified risk opportunities are not being acted upon, leaving potential RAF value and associated care management insights unrealized.

Risk recapture rate YoY.definition: The year-over-year percentage change in the risk recapture rate for each churn status segment, tracking whether gap closure efficiency is trending positively or negatively.
Risk recapture rate YoY.increasing: Improvement year-over-year suggests that outreach, coding, and clinical documentation programs are gaining traction within the segment.
Risk recapture rate YoY.decreasing: Decline year-over-year signals that gap closure capacity or provider responsiveness has weakened relative to the prior period, warranting program review.

Open gaps (Dropped).definition: The count of HCC conditions that were coded in a prior period but have not yet been re-documented in the current year for members in each churn status segment, representing lapsed diagnosis gaps.
Open gaps (Dropped).increasing: More dropped gaps indicate that previously confirmed chronic conditions are not being recaptured, increasing the risk of RAF score decline and potential care continuity issues.
Open gaps (Dropped).decreasing: Fewer dropped gaps mean the plan is successfully re-documenting lapsed conditions, preserving RAF scores and ensuring continuity of chronic disease management.

Open gaps (Suspected).definition: The count of HCC conditions that clinical evidence or predictive models suggest are present but have not yet been coded or confirmed for members in each churn status segment.
Open gaps (Suspected).increasing: A growing number of suspected gaps signals a larger untapped risk documentation opportunity, but also potential under-diagnosis or insufficient provider engagement in that segment.
Open gaps (Suspected).decreasing: Fewer suspected gaps indicate that clinically implied conditions are being investigated and coded, reducing unconfirmed risk and improving the completeness of the member's health record.
